projects.name: DRAFTRON
highlights: Built a LangGraph cover-letter generation agent with interrupt()-based Human-in-the-Loop checkpoints, allowing users to review and redirect the workflow before final generation.

Architected cost-aware model routing that uses Groq Llama 3.3 70B for extraction, matching, strategy, and critique, while reserving GPT-5 mini for draft generation and revision to optimize quality and API cost.
Designed the core graph with explicit start() and resume() methods from the beginning, making it reusable as a callable sub-agent inside future multi-agent supervisor architectures.

projects.name: LAPIS — Multi-Agent AI Voice Tutor for a Virtual Chemistry Lab
highlights: Architected a three-agent LiveKit system (Coordinator, LabTutor, Researcher) that shares session state and performs real-time agent handoffs while enforcing a strict sequential laboratory workflow.
Built a real-time Egyptian-Arabic voice tutor using Google Gemini Live speech-to-speech, a Simli lip-synced avatar, and a lightweight RAG pipeline powered by OpenAI embeddings and cosine similarity.

Designed an 11-method RPC protocol over LiveKit data channels to synchronize the browser-based chemistry lab with the AI backend, including automatic grading through numeric tolerance validation and similarity-based observation matching.

The project was preceded by a resource-constrained edge AI prototype using OpenAI Whisper, on-device Mistral inference, and HX711 sensor telemetry, whose latency and hardware lessons directly influenced the final multi-agent architecture.

projects.name: Agentic RAG Research Assistant
highlights: Designed a stateful LangGraph workflow with three retrieval modes — local FAISS RAG, live Tavily web search, and hybrid retrieval — controlled by an LLM-powered Query Analyzer.
Implemented automatic inline citation generation and a dedicated summarization node to produce source-grounded research answers with reduced hallucination risk.
Engineered zero-code-change configurability between local Ollama and cloud OpenAI backends for cost-aware deployment switching.

projects.name: Multimodal Enterprise Knowledge System
highlights: Engineered a multimodal RAG architecture that ingests PDFs, images, and DOCX files into a unified FAISS vector store for retrieval across heterogeneous knowledge sources.
Built an intelligent model-routing layer that dynamically selects the least expensive capable model, reducing API token cost by approximately 40%.
Optimized document ingestion with asynchronous processing, significantly reducing latency for large knowledge bases.
